assessment.diversity_evidence: All 20 stories use the same core premise and outcome: a child rescues a small animal stranded on a high ledge with a ladder, then warms it in a cottage. The only meaningful causal variation is whether the child acts independently (group 0; e.g. s000029, s000076) or asks an adult for advice or the ladder (group 1; e.g. s000073, s000070). Failed reaching and whether the child fetches or climbs the ladder are minor branches, not substantially different plots. Endings and language remain highly similar across the set.

plot_groups.summary: The child independently recognizes or obtains a ladder, sometimes after an unsuccessful reach, and uses it to bring the stranded animal down before warming it indoors.
The child asks an adult for help or advice; the adult recommends and sometimes brings the ladder, which the child uses to rescue the stranded animal and warm it indoors.

assessment.diversity_evidence: All twenty stories concern repairing a torn kite so it can fly again. Most follow the same repair-and-launch sequence, with minor variation in whether the child figures out the tape alone (s000057, s000043, s000009, s000042) or gets adult advice and supplies (s000047, s000073, s000034). Three add a failed launch before repair (s000029, s000068, s000088). All end with the repaired kite flying, so outcomes and language remain highly repetitive. These sampled stories do not establish the diversity of the whole generator.

The child independently recognizes or uses tape to mend the torn kite, then launches the repaired kite successfully.
The child seeks adult advice or help obtaining tape, repairs the torn kite, and gets it flying again.

assessment.diversity_evidence: All twenty stories share the same central problem and outcome: a locked cottage, a missing key under a dark bench, lantern-assisted discovery, and entry. The main causal variation is whether the child independently realizes light will help (s000029, s000096) or asks an adult who suggests or supplies the lantern (s000057, s000068); some include an unsuccessful search first (s000043, s000049). Thanks and minor wording changes do not create new plot structures. This sample is highly repetitive and does not establish the generator’s broader diversity.

plot_groups.summary: The child independently recognizes or uses the lantern to illuminate the dark hiding place, finds the key, and opens the cottage.
The child seeks an adult’s help or advice, obtains or is given the lantern, finds the key under the bench, and opens the cottage.
